title: Exponential Growth and Epidemics (COVID-19)
hook: Opens directly on the real COVID-19 case data plotted as an accelerating curve, letting the alarming shape speak before any explanation begins.

scenes.purpose: Ground the abstract topic in urgent, real data before defining anything

on_screen.desc: Live dot-by-dot animation of COVID-19 case counts, y-axis rescaling twice as numbers overflow
Title: 'Recorded COVID-19 cases outside mainland China'
Running integer counter next to moving dot showing current case count
Pink arc lines with ×1.15–1.25 multiplier labels between successive dots

scenes.transition: Axes kept; multiplier labels fade out entering next scene
scenes.narration_gist: The data for COVID-19 cases is shown growing day by day, with each step being roughly 1.15–1.25 times the previous.

scenes.purpose: Introduce the four questions that structure the whole video

on_screen.desc: Four questions fading in one at a time: What is it? Where does it come from? What does it imply? When does it stop?

scenes.transition: Questions fade out downward in a lagged sweep; clean slate for the model
scenes.narration_gist: Four questions frame the lesson: definition, origin, implication, and endpoint of exponential growth.

scenes.purpose: Show the mechanism—infected people exposing neighbors—before writing any equation

on_screen.desc: Grid of 150 Randolph pi-creatures; one turns sickly green as patient zero
Flash bursts radiating from infected figures each round
Newly infected creatures change color in staggered waves

scenes.transition: Simulation clears; equation variables appear at top
scenes.narration_gist: A visual simulation shows each infected person exposing nearby neighbors, making it viscerally clear why existing cases drive new cases.

scenes.purpose: Formalize the mechanism into an equation, building it term by term

on_screen.desc: Three color-coded variable definitions: N (yellow), E (blue), p (teal)
ΔN_d = E·p·N_d built by TransformFromCopy of each variable label
Factored form N_{d+1} = (1 + E·p)·N_d with brace showing '1.15'
Closed-form N_d = (1+E·p)^d · N_0 with arrow from factored form

scenes.transition: Equation group shifts left; EP factor gets red rectangle highlight kept on screen
scenes.narration_gist: The daily change equals E·p·N, so tomorrow's total is just today's multiplied by a constant greater than one.

scenes.purpose: Make the exponential legible by switching to a log scale and fitting a line

on_screen.desc: Original dot data animating upward to log-spaced positions; y-axis relabels 10, 100, 1k … 1B
'Logarithmic scale' subtitle in teal
Teal regression line through the dots labeled '×10 every 16 days'
R² value counting up to ~0.999 inside a highlighted box

scenes.transition: R² box fades; camera zooms out to reveal extended x-axis
scenes.narration_gist: On a log scale the data falls almost perfectly on a straight line, and linear regression confirms the fit is 'really freaking close.'

scenes.purpose: Show the terrifying forward projection of the straight line extended in time

on_screen.desc: Regression line extended 90 more days on zoomed-out log axes
Expanding teal rectangles marking 30/47/64/81 days to 1M/10M/100M/1B
Date labels (Apr 5, Apr 22, May 9, May 26) ticking up at each milestone

scenes.transition: Rectangle and label fade right; two hypothetical projected-dot paths appear then fade
scenes.narration_gist: Extending the line predicts one million cases in 30 days, a billion in 81—viscerally illustrating why the trend cannot continue.

scenes.purpose: Introduce the logistic curve: exponential is just its early segment

on_screen.desc: S-shaped logistic curve drawn in yellow over a plain time axis
Red exponential curve overlaid on the early portion inside a teal shaded region
Inflection point dot with label; tangent line sweeping along the curve showing slope change
ODE dN/dt = c(1 − N/pop)·N shown in upper right

scenes.transition: ODE fades; growth-factor fraction appears beside inflection point
scenes.narration_gist: Every exponential is the opening of a logistic curve; the inflection point is where new daily cases peak and the growth factor drops to one.

scenes.purpose: Teach the growth-factor diagnostic: distinguish GF>1 from GF≈1 in real numbers

on_screen.desc: Column of recent case totals with dates (Mar 3–6)
Column of daily changes in green with curved arrows between totals
Growth-factor fractions (change_d / change_{d-1}) animating to show GF=1.15 vs GF=1.0
Section headers: Totals / Changes / Growth factors

scenes.transition: Table stays; new projection calculation slides in to the right
scenes.narration_gist: A growth factor only slightly above 1 looks innocuous in the totals column but signals orders-of-magnitude growth still ahead.

scenes.purpose: Show dramatic sensitivity of outcome to small changes in the growth rate

on_screen.desc: Equation (1.15)^61 · 21,000 = ~100 million counting up
Equation (1.05)^61 · 21,000 = ~400,000 counting up below
Animated decimal toggling between 1.15 and 1.05 next to 'E·p factor'
Mortimer character with speech bubble: 'The only thing to fear is the lack of fear itself'

scenes.transition: Final hold on both equations side by side with character visible
scenes.narration_gist: Dropping the daily growth rate from 15% to 5% reduces a 61-day projection from 100 million to 400,000—so collective worry is the lever.

lessons: Lead with real, emotionally charged data before introducing any abstraction—let the phenomenon earn the theory.
Use a physical simulation (creatures spreading infection) to build intuition for a mechanism before formalizing it as an equation.
Construct equations on screen term by term using TransformFromCopy of previously defined variables, so the formula feels discovered rather than imposed.
When data spans orders of magnitude, animate the rescaling to a log axis in-place so viewers experience the transformation rather than just seeing the result.
Zoom the camera out to extend a graph's time axis for projections, preserving context while revealing the frightening forward trajectory.

Place a comparative diagnostic table (totals vs. changes vs. growth factors) across left/center/right zones so each conceptual layer occupies its own column, making the relationship spatially legible.
End with a concrete numerical contrast—same formula, two inputs, wildly different outputs—so the practical stakes of the math land in a single closing image.
